title: Frames now come from the 1080p proxy at full size: about twice the local VLM's image tokens, and 8- and 9-frame windows go past the 16k context
where: broll/indexer/broll_index/ffmpeg_tools.py:821 (extract_frames, no scale); pipeline.py:211 (_frames_source); ffmpeg_tools.py:312 (PROXY_HEIGHT 1080); local_vlm.py:46-47; config.py:255
what: The local backend was tuned on 960x540 frames (~1,024 tokens each after the minimum). Since 2026-09-17 frames are cut from the 1080p proxy at native size, ~2,040 Qwen3-VL tokens each, so a 9-frame window is ~18.4k+1k tokens against a 16,384-token slot.
cost: Every clip whose balanced window has 8-9 frames (e.g. 8-9 or 15-18 frames, ~30-36 s or 60-72 s at max_gap 4 s) gets HTTP 400, raised as LocalVlmError, which matches no fatal marker, so the clip is marked 'error' and the queue moves on. Even if capped: ~2x encode_ms (2.7 s -> ~5.4 s per 7-frame window), and 3.2x JPEG bytes per frame on 401k+ kept frames.
evidence: usage.jsonl: 7 frames = 8,473 / 8 frames = 9,531 input tokens at 960x540; server log n_ctx_slot 16384, --image-min-tokens 1024; video 25438 frames 960x540, proxy and newest proxies 1920x1080; last local run predates the 1080p re-encode; probe 99 vs 31 KiB/frame. Model not loaded (brief rule).
fix: Scale frames in extract_frames (-vf scale='min(960,iw)':-2) so frames match the eval regardless of proxy height; keep the (timestamp,path) pairing. Optionally treat 'exceeds the available context' as run-fatal.

title: The packet count that costs a second full NAS read of every original is already printed by the proxy encode
what: _bad() demuxes the whole original over SMB (ffprobe -count_packets) for the exact frame check; the encode already reads every source packet, and at -loglevel verbose prints 'Input stream #0:0 (video): N packets read'. The verify decode likewise prints dest packets and decode errors. The source is also ffprobed 3 times per clip.
cost: Per clip: ~200 MB extra read (~4.3 s at 46 MB/s); ~6-8 h of NAS read per back-catalogue pass of 5-7k clips, ~60 h at 50k (estimated), shared across the parallel_local workers.
evidence: Probe: verbose encode summary '1800 packets read; 1800 frames decoded; 0 decode errors' equals ffprobe nb_read_packets 1800 on the same file.
ledger: related to CR-286B / broll-indexer-1 (fixed; names 'a count carried forward' as the way back)
fix: Parse src/dst counts and decode errors from the encode and verify passes' verbose summaries; keep frames_match exact and 'both known or skip'; change the companion twin and parity tests in the same commit; count_frames_cmd as fallback.

title: The API describe path never hits the prompt cache: the ~3k-token instruction block sits after the images, with the per-window sheet list near its top
what: Every call is [4 images][prompt]; the images and the sheet list (line 12 of 226) vary per window, so no stable prefix exists and no cache_control is set.
cost: ~2 calls/clip, ~10k calls per 5k-clip archive; ~2.7k of ~7k input tokens could bill at 0.1x, ~35-40% of input spend (~$50 per 10k calls on sonnet-5, estimated). The Haiku 4.5 minimum is 4,096 tokens, so it caches only if the prefix clears that.
evidence: Code read: no system block or cache_control anywhere in broll/indexer.
fix: Put the fixed instructions plus taxonomy in a system block with cache_control; keep images then the sheet list in the user turn; verify cache_read_input_tokens > 0 on the second call.

title: Offline backfill pays full price: the Message Batches API (half price) is not used
what: The overnight API stage drives synchronous calls through workers, semaphores and rate-limit sleeps; the Batches API does the same work asynchronously at 50% of the token price.
cost: Anthropic backend only (opt-in): ~$0.02-0.03 saved per call, ~$200-300 per 10k calls (estimated), stacking with caching.
fix: Add a --batch mode: custom_id video:window, submit, poll, merge per video, write as now; clips stay 'proxied' until complete.

title: anthropic.max_tokens 8000 sits below a third of the archive's historical outputs; a truncated answer costs two paid calls and then marks the clip error
what: stop_reason max_tokens only logs; the truncated JSON fails to parse, the window is re-asked at the same ceiling (paid twice), then the clip is marked error. Unused headroom is free.
cost: Historical haiku output: median 5,961, p90 12,783, p99 20,313; 2,915/8,996 (32%) over 8,000 - if visible output rather than CLI thinking, ~1/3 of windows truncate.
fix: Default to 16000; on max_tokens retry once with a doubled ceiling.

title: The cost estimate and alias table lag the price list: sonnet-5 is costed 50% high
what: PRICE_PER_MTOK has claude-sonnet-5 at $3/$15; the current price is $2/$10. Current-generation models are absent from the alias table.
cost: Every usage.jsonl forecast for the default model overstates cost by 50%.
evidence: Code read against the current model/price table.
fix: Correct the row and add current models; update the doc table in the same change.

title: usage.jsonl takes concurrent appends without a lock; the live file has a torn line, and the documented forecast snippet crashes on it
what: N threads (and a second --after-id process) open-append per call; one line in the live file is the fragment 'n_ms": 25423}', and the doc's json.loads-per-line forecast raises on it.
cost: 1 torn line of 12,705; the recommended forecast fails outright until the file is hand-edited.
evidence: My parse of the live usage.jsonl failed at line 8716.
fix: Single os.write per record on an O_APPEND fd under a lock; make the snippet skip bad lines.

title: An account-wide stop in the middle of a clip throws away the windows already paid for
what: Window results live only in memory until the final write; FatalRunError on window k drops windows 1..k-1 and the rerun pays for them again.
cost: Up to (windows-1) calls per in-flight clip per stop; tens of calls on a night of repeated limits (estimated).
fix: Persist each parsed window as sheets/<id>/window_<k>.json keyed by sheets and model; reuse on rerun; delete after the write.

title: A rescan writes and commits every unchanged file
what: A known, same-size file still goes through upsert_video: a second lookup, an UPDATE with identical values and a commit.
cost: 1.12 ms/file measured: ~5 s per 4,482-file share, ~9 min per 500k files of pure commits.
fix: Skip the write when hash/size/in_inbox already match; batch the rest per directory or per 500 rows.

title: A music sweep with nothing changed still loads CLAP onto the GPU and re-scores the whole library
what: The full sweep loads the CLAP model before computing todo and always retags; the --queue path already skips the retag when nothing was added.
cost: Per manual sweep: seconds of model load, ~1 GB VRAM beside Resolve, and a whole-library rescore for zero changes.
fix: Compute todo first; with nothing to analyse, prune or close, exit before loading CLAP.
